This class of compounds is known to interact with Ppara, a key enzyme involved in lipid metabolism. The structural similarity between Bezafibrate and Clofibrate, which binds to Ppara, implies a potential mechanism of action where Bezafibrate may also interact with Ppara through a similar binding site. The low common ancestor between Bezafibrate and Clofibrate, along with the shared pathway to fibrate antilipidemic agents, supports the hypothesis that Bezafibrate could exert its effects on Ppara via a mechanism that is not yet fully elucidated. This integrated explanation highlights the importance of structural similarity and shared pharmacological pathways in predicting drug-target interactions.
